observation.visible_scene: A dance studio with a full mirror wall, horizontal ballet barres, a wrapped pillar, and a pale floor. A woman seen from behind (black short-sleeve top, pink flared pants, hair in a bun) stands center; her masked front-facing figure in the mirror is her reflection, not a second person. A phone lies on the floor near the mirror base and stays put throughout.
visible_changes: At the start she balances on her left leg with the right foot lifted and crossed behind, both arms bent with hands raised to shoulder/head height in a finger gesture.

Over roughly t=0 to t=0.5 s the lifted right foot lowers until the legs are crossed (right foot tucked behind the left ankle), and she settles into a crossed-leg standing position that she holds for the rest of the clip.

Around t=0.6–1.0 s her right arm transitions from the bent raised position to fully extended forward/up toward the mirror with a flat open palm; this extended pose is held from about t=1.0 s to the end (t=2.67 s).
Her left arm, bent and raised early on, drops to her side and is largely hidden by her torso during the later frames.
The hand shape changes from a pointed/claw-like gesture (early frames) to an open flat palm on the extended right hand.
The camera is stationary: the mirror seams, pillar, barres, and floor phone keep the same positions; only the dancer and her reflection move.
The reflection mirrors all of the above: it shows the same leg-lowering, the same arm extension (appearing as the reflection's left arm reaching toward the glass), and the same hand-shape change.
outside_clip_unknowns: What precedes the opening one-leg pose and what follows the held arm-extension (the segment ends mid-pose).
Whether the body rotation/hip angle is part of a turn that continues outside the crop.
The music or cue driving the movements.
uncertain_details: Exact finger configuration in the early hand gesture is hard to resolve.
A slight change in torso/hip orientation between early and late frames is visible but its cause (a small turn vs. pose shift) is not determinable.
Precise moment of full leg-cross completion is approximate.
